## What we got from our local land grant

As a farm family, we got many useful things from Virginia Tech and its
extension service: 

- Evidence basis and demonstration of best practices
- Documents that provided guidance: "helpfiles"
- Recipes!
- Training to make the best, safest use of available tools

Overall, we got information and training that was **based on good science**, **free**, 
**practical**, and ready to **use right away**. 

# Open-source software

## R programming language

The R programming language is **free and open-source software**. 

```{r echo = FALSE, out.width = "\\textwidth", fig.align = "center"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/cran_base_r.png")
```

## Base R

When you initially install R, you are getting **base R**, which is a fairly 
basic set of tools for working with data. 

```{r echo = FALSE, out.width = "0.65\\textwidth", fig.align = "center"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/BrioBasicSet.jpg")
```

\vspace{-1cm}
\footnotesize Source: Brio

## R Package Ecosystem

**Packages** extend base R to do all kinds of different things, and they can
be created and shared by anyone. 

```{r echo = FALSE, out.width = "\\textwidth"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/BrioFancySet.jpg")
```

\vspace{-1cm}
\footnotesize Source: Brio

## R Package Ecosystem

There are over 20,000 packages on the primary repository alone. 

```{r echo = FALSE, out.width = "0.8\\textwidth", fig.align = "center"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/use_r_aust_hexbins_closeup.jpg")
```

\footnotesize Mitchell O'Hara-Wild: https://www.mitchelloharawild.com/blog/user-2018-feature-wall/

# Groundhog Day

## Groundhog Day

\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
\textbf{Groundhog Day: February 2}

\medskip

If a grandhog sees its shadow, there will be six more weeks of winter. 
If not, there will be an early spring.

## Groundhog Day

We'll use this as an example of open-source software and how a scientist 
can use it for some of the key tasks in making sense of all the data out 
there in the world: 

- **Gather**
- Integrate
- Explore
- Analyze
- **Communicate**

## ERHS 535---R Programming for Research

R Programming for Research (ERHS 535) has been taken by students pursuing 
degrees in: 

Environmental Health, Cellular \& Molecular Biology, 
Public Health, Microbiology, Clinical Sciences, Animal Sciences, 
Mechanical Engineering, Ecology, Radiological Health Sciences, 
Biochemistry, Food Science \& Nutrition, Pathology, 
Human Development \& Family Studies, Civil \& Environmental Engineering, 
Ecosystem Sustainability, Fish Wildlife and Conservation Biology, 
Forest Sciences, Soil \& Crop Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Horticulture, 
Data Analysis, Civil Engineering, Mathematics, and Chemistry
